summary: A file re-created at a rename's old path escapes lanes. touchedFiles keeps the R entry's renamedFrom, but the new untracked file at that path becomes status A. buildGraph now drops every extraFiles path from 'all' even when it exists, so the new file is neither a test nor scanned. removedPath then waives it as 'old name of <new>'. Reproduced on a fixture: after a committed mv test/util.test.js -> test/util2.test.js plus an untracked failing test/util.test.js, lanes reported pass, ran only util2, and printed 'removed (no lane owed): test/util.test.js — old name of test/util2.test.js'. The same happened for a source file (lib/util.js) re-created after its rename. Before this diff, ls-files listed the file, so it ran as a test or failed as no-lane.
fix: Treat a path as gone only when it is absent from the working tree. Filter gone and extraFiles with lstat (or by excluding paths that are also in touched with status A or M), and have removedPath refuse a file that exists. Add a regression test for a re-created old name.

summary: A deleted non-test file that remaining code still imports is waived with 'no remaining test references it' (the docs say 'nothing left to test'). The reverse graph has the dangling edge, but testsFor only looks for tests, so an untested importer keeps a broken require and the check passes. Reproduced on a fixture: base lib/consumer.js requires ./util.js; deleting lib/util.js and its test gave pass with 'nothing touched selects a test; 2 removed path(s)'. Before this diff the file was PREGATE_NO_LANE. This narrows the gate under uncertainty, against the module's 'every uncertainty widens the selection' rule.
fix: In removedPath, when graph.reverse.get(file) still has present non-test dependents, fail closed (or name them as 'still imported by <x>' and keep the file in noLane). Add a fixture test with an untested importer.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] Resolver blindness is reported as "exercised no file" and passes the gate. lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:119 and lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:506. goneSubjects is computed only through referencesIn (JS/TS imports, Python imports, Dart, test-tree literals) plus conventionBins. It ignores rustEdges, djangoEdges, `dependencies` declarations, and anything the resolver cannot see. referencesIn also gets `unresolved = undefined`, so specifiers that resolve to nothing are thrown away instead of recorded. Take a deleted `foo_test.go` (import-graph has no Go import resolution), a `_spec.rb` or `.bats` test that reaches its subject by a non-literal path, or a JS test with an alias the resolver misses. Each one yields an empty subjects list, gets the note `it exercised no file still in the tree`, and owes no lane. Before this branch, the same deletion reached noLane and failed PREGATE_NO_LANE. So a fail-closed path is now fail-open, and the note states something false: it claims the test exercised nothing when the graph simply could not see what it exercised. Deleting a regression test for a guard written in one of those languages passes pregate silently, and lostCoverage stays empty, so the detail line says nothing either. Fix: pass an `unresolved` array into the goneSources referencesIn call. When subjects are empty and (a) unresolved is non-empty, or (b) the file's language has no forward resolution (go/rb/bats), return null so it fails closed like an unreadable merge-base text.

label: FIXABLE
summary: [FIXABLE] A deleted test named only in a `dependencies` mapping silently drops its declared subjects. lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:503-508 and lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:117-131. Projects add declarations exactly where the graph cannot see a test's subjects (for example `"lib/x/**": ["test/x.test.ts"]`). goneSubjects never looks at `opts.declarations`, so deleting `test/x.test.ts` leaves lib/x/** out of lostCoverage. It reports `it exercised no file still in the tree` (or lists only its import subjects) and passes, and the stale declaration stays in .gstack/pregate.json pointing at a file that no longer exists. Fix: add every file that matches a glob whose declared list contains the removed test to that test's subjects, and flag the stale declaration.

summary: [FIXABLE] A rename's old path that has been recreated is still treated as gone. lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:136 and lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:478. `gone` includes every `renamedFrom`, and buildGraph now filters those paths out of `all`. Consider a committed rename a->b followed by a new untracked `a` in the working tree (context.ts:126-130 keeps both entries). The new `a` is never scanned for imports, and if it is a test it is dropped from graph.tests. In the seed loop, testsFor(a) finds nothing, `gone.includes(a)` is true, and removedPath returns `old name of b`, so the new file owes no lane and its test never runs. Fix: exclude from `gone` any path that is also a touched non-D path (`touchedByPath.get(p)?.status !== 'D'`) or that exists on disk.

label: High
summary: High — Deleting a Rust module can pass without compiling its crate. Location: lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:477-478,496; lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:116,200-205. The graph removes every deleted path from `all`, then calls `rustEdges(all, ...)`. Rust dependencies are supplied by that crate-level graph, not by the JS/Python import scanner, so a deleted `.rs` module has no edge to its surviving crate tests. The new removed-path exemption then passes it as “no remaining test references it.” For example, delete `src/required.rs` while leaving `mod required;` and unit tests in `src/lib.rs`: the crate no longer compiles, but this selection schedules no test and owes no lane. An in-memory call using the actual `rustEdges` and `testsFor` returned remaining tests `["src/lib.rs"]` but an empty selection for `src/required.rs`. Preserve deleted Rust paths as dependency nodes in the Cargo graph while excluding them from runnable tests; deletion must still select the surviving crate tests.

label: Medium
summary: Medium — Directory dependencies disappear when reconstructing a deleted test's subjects. Location: lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:506-507. `referencesIn` represents directory reads as `dir/**`, but the new `present.has(t)` filter only accepts literal file paths. A deleted test that enumerated or validated `lib/widgets` therefore loses all of its subjects: the actual resolver returns `lib/widgets/**`, then this filter drops it even when `lib/widgets/a.js` remains. The deletion is reported as “it exercised no file still in the tree,” no surviving tests of those files run, and removal of their last test is not reported. This silently bypasses the promised owning-suite and lost-coverage checks for directory-based tests. Expand directory targets to their present member files before filtering and selecting suites.

Fail-closed path for an unreadable deleted test is covered only for the over-1-MiB case. The docs and the provenance line also promise fail-closed for a symlink and for invalid UTF-8, and neither has a test. readAtMergeBase now accepts a mode list, so a regression that admits 120000 blobs would turn a deleted symlinked test into a silent pass.

summary: A path the branch re-created at a rename's old name is classed as 'removed (no lane owed)' and is never selected, so the lanes gate goes green on a failing test. `gone` (line 136) takes every `renamedFrom` without checking that the path is really absent. buildGraph (import-graph.ts:478) now drops every extraFile from `all`, so the re-created file is never scanned and never enters graph.tests. Then `gone.includes(file)` sends it to removedPath, which returns 'old name of <new>'. Reproduced on a scratch fixture: `git mv test/util.test.js test/math.test.js`, either committed or only staged, followed by a new untracked test/util.test.js with a failing assertion. At head, lanes reports status=pass with 'removed (no lane owed): test/util.test.js — old name of test/math.test.js' and 'ran: node --test test/math.test.js'. At base 6f27f0c2 the same fixture runs both files and fails with 1 failed of 2. A re-created non-test file with no lane (for example a compatibility shim left at the old path) passes the same way instead of failing with PREGATE_NO_LANE. Remote pregate runs only the selected files, so a READY can carry a false green.
fix: Treat a path as gone only when it is absent from the working tree: build `gone` from paths that fail fs.existsSync, or drop any renamedFrom that also appears as a touched A/M entry. Filter by the same rule in buildGraph so a present file is still scanned and still counts as a test. Add a regression test: a rename followed by an untracked file at the old name must select and run that file.

summary: [FIXABLE, high] A deleted test whose subjects the graph cannot see passes with a false claim. lane-selection.ts:119 turns `subjects.length === 0` into "it exercised no file still in the tree" with zero tests owed. But goneSubjects (import-graph.ts:505-507) comes only from referencesIn() plus conventionBins(). referencesIn() parses JS/TS, Python and Dart imports and otherwise only quoted literals or join() runs. So a deleted `_test.go`, `_test.rb`, `_spec.rb` or `.bats` test, a Django test whose edges come from djangoEdges, or a JS test that builds its target path from variables all produce an empty subject list. That turns a former PREGATE_NO_LANE into a silent pass, and the provenance asserts something the graph never established. Fix: treat empty subjects as unknown (return null, which fails closed like the unreadable case) unless the deleted test's language is one referencesIn parses and at least one reference resolved. At the very least, reword the note to "no subject the import graph could see" and exclude it from the pass path.

summary: [FIXABLE, medium] buildGraph now drops live files that appear in `gone`. import-graph.ts:478 removes every extraFiles path from `all`, and lane-selection.ts:136 puts every `renamedFrom` into `gone`. Two real states make renamedFrom a file that still exists: (a) context.ts:117 maps git's `C` (copy) status to `R` with renamedFrom. Under a user's `diff.renames=copies` config, `git diff -M` reports copies, so the copy source is still on disk. (b) A committed rename A→B followed by an uncommitted re-creation of A gives a `??` entry with status A for A, while A is still B's renamedFrom. In both cases the live file is no longer scanned for edges and is removed from graph.tests, so a live test there is never selected. The file itself then reaches removedPath at line 114, gets "old name of B" and owes no lane. Before this diff, `all` still held it. Fix: build `gone` only from paths absent from the working tree, for example by filtering out any path that has its own touched entry with status A or M or that exists on disk. Also stop mapping `C` to a rename with a gone source.

summary: [INVESTIGATE, low] The cache key and cost were not updated for the new data. - The lanes `inputs` (lanes.ts:507) hash only the test selection, so two trees whose removed or lostCoverage sets differ but whose selection is the same share an input identity, and a reused result can carry a stale detail. - readAtMergeBase makes two sequential git spawns per deleted test, each with a 60 s timeout. label: High
summary: **High — Deleted Rust modules bypass their crate's test lane.** `lib/pregate/lane-selection.ts:116,197–204` waives a removed non-test file when the graph selects nothing, but `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:478,496` removes that path before constructing Cargo dependency edges. For a crate with `src/lib.rs` containing `mod foo;` and an existing unit test, deleting `src/foo.rs` therefore selects no tests and is reported as “no remaining test references it.” The crate no longer compiles, yet the tests stage can pass without invoking Cargo. The pure `rustEdges()` comparison confirms that supplying the removed path restores its `src/foo.rs → Cargo.toml → src/lib.rs` lane. Preserve removed Rust files as dependency nodes while excluding them from runnable tests; add a regression for deleting a module still declared by the crate.

label: Medium
summary: **Medium — Deleting the last file in a referenced directory silently skips its surviving test.** `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:480–481` builds directory names only from remaining files, even though removed file names are retained in `files`. A surviving test using `readdirSync('fixtures/scenarios')` loses its `fixtures/scenarios/**` dependency when the branch deletes that directory's last tracked file. `removedPath()` then waives the deletion instead of selecting the test or failing closed. That test would fail with ENOENT, but the tests stage can certify the deletion without running it. Calling `referencesIn()` with the remaining directory set returns no edge; preserving the removed file's parent directories returns the expected wildcard edge. Build dependency-directory nodes from both current and removed paths, and cover last-file directory deletion, including unstaged deletion.

label: Medium
summary: **Medium — Deleted-test subject extraction drops directory dependencies and product code reached through helpers.** `lib/pregate/import-graph.ts:505–507` takes only direct references, then requires every target to be a present concrete file outside the test tree. A deleted test that reads `lib/pkg` produces the target `lib/pkg/**`, which this filter always discards. A deleted test that calls `test/helpers/exercise.ts`, which imports `lib/util.ts`, also produces no subject because the helper is discarded without following its imports. Both paths reach `lane-selection.ts:119`, claiming “it exercised no file still in the tree,” even when surviving tests exercise those product files; their owning suite is not selected, and actual last-test losses are not reported. Pure resolver calls confirm both empty subject sets. Expand directory targets and traverse dependencies through helpers before excluding helpers from the reported subject list; test both remaining-suite selection and last-coverage reporting.
